title: 73,000 Doctors Have Applied for Mexico’s Primary Health Care Clinics Initiative
author: Emir Olivares and Alma E. Muñoz
content:
_This article by[Emir Olivares and Alma E.
Muñoz](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Emir%20Olivares%20y%20Alma%20E.%20Mu%C3%B1oz)
originally appeared in the [October 6, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/10/06/sociedad/se-han-
postulado-73-mil-medicos-para-la-iniciativa-gubernamental-consultorios-de-
atencion-primaria-a-la-salud), Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

So far, **73,000 health professionals have applied** to be part of the federal
government's Primary Health Care Clinics initiative, reported the
Undersecretary of Sectoral Integration and Development of the Secretariat of
Health, Eduardo Clark, who said that the call for hiring will close in a
little over ten days.

At the mañanera he said that the goal of this project is to have **12,750
points of care for non-serious illnesses** in the 24 states where IMSS-
Bienestar operates.

> We are going to universalize this model of care, there will be no
> rejections, people will be treated regardless of their social security
> entitlement.
>
> Eduardo Clark, Undersecretary of Health

Currently, he said, the clinics are in the process of being fitted out and
staff hired, and they are expected to **begin operating starting in January**.

In that regard, the federal head of state said that these health care spaces
will be located both in cities and in the most remote places in the country.

“The idea is that if there is no serious illness, you go to the clinic, you
would be treated free of charge and you will have your medicines, 60 basic
medicines to be able to treat the main things. If the doctor realizes that
greater care is needed, you will be referred to the hospital.”

Meanwhile, reporting on the progress of the Health House to House program, the
head of the Secretariat of Well-being, Leticia Ramírez, indicated that **more
than 27 million home medical consultations** have been provided to
beneficiaries of the pensions for older adults and people with disabilities.

Of that total, 12,806,540 people have had a first visit, 8,305,567 two visits
and 5,954,767 up to a third.

“This shows that it is not an isolated visit, it is accompaniment, follow-up
and prevention.” To date, she said, 10,276,651 homes have been visited.

In that framework, the Undersecretary of Well-being, Jesús Salvador Valencia,
said that through these visits of the Health House to House program, 568,800
patients with high blood pressure have been detected and referred to the IMSS
for care, 117,000 more to IMSS-Bienestar, 161,000 to the ISSSTE and 5,600 to
Pemex.

Likewise, 147,661 patients with diabetes were sent to the IMSS, 37,304 to
IMSS-Bienestar, 40,559 to the ISSSTE and 557 to Pemex hospitals.
